title: The Protocol of Vienna
premise: Wren Thornbury, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Section — an embassy that exists only in sealed ledgers — is assigned to extract Dr. Ilse Marchetti, a defector whose testimony could burn three governments. But Flight VA-214, the plane meant to carry her out, vanishes from every record while still airborne, and Wren realizes the flight was never real: it's a trap built from forged memory, designed to make Wren the fall figure for an assassination. As the Vienna border checkpoint prepares its midnight shift change — the only window when identities go unverified — Wren must decide whether Ilse is a genuine defector or the bait, and whether their own past, which the Section has carefully rewritten, can be trusted. In the end, Wren trades their own erased identity to the Section's archivist in exchange for Ilse's safe crossing, walking through the checkpoint as no one at all — belonging to nothing, and finally free of the lie.
about_author: Jude Okonkwo is a former diplomatic courier who spent a decade shuttling between Vienna, Geneva, and cities that preferred not to be named. They write thrillers about the people history files under 'administrative error.'

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Erasures
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A routine cleanup: scrubbing a diplomat's affair from three databases in a Vienna café that never appears on maps. Wren is competent, invisible, and quietly aching with the sense that their own file is thinner than it should be. The beat is controlled loneliness — a professional who has erased themselves by habit.

chapters.title: Flight VA-214
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Summoned at dawn: Flight VA-214, carrying a sealed diplomatic pouch, has vanished from every flight-tracking system, manifest, and air-traffic log — yet radar confirms it's still circling over Lower Austria. Wren is ordered to intercept the passenger list. The beat is vertigo: the world's records disagreeing with reality, and Wren realizing they're already implicated.

chapters.title: The Woman with Two Birthdays
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Dr. Ilse Marchetti waits in a safehouse, rehearsing a life story that contains one deliberate flaw — a birthday that doesn't exist in any registry. She knows she's being tested, and she knows someone is coming for her. The beat is coiled patience: a defector who understands that identity is a performance she must get exactly right.

chapters.title: Paper Trail of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Digging into VA-214, Wren finds the forgery is exquisite — stamped with protocols only the Section itself uses. Someone inside is framing them. Their handler, Vasik, offers reassurance that feels like a noose being measured. The beat is paranoia sharpening into resolve: Wren decides to run the extraction off-book.

chapters.title: Coffee with the Archivist
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren tracks down Frau Heller, the Section's retired archivist, who keeps the true records the databases can't touch. Heller reveals a fragment of Wren's own original file — a name, a hometown, a first betrayal — and warns that whoever built the fake flight also built the fake Wren. The beat is grief: memory as contraband.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren and Ilse finally meet, and each privately concludes the other might be the trap. Ilse offers her real intelligence — proof of the assassination plot the phantom flight is meant to enable — but only if Wren gets her across the border tonight. The beat is mutual suspicion curdling into reluctant trust.

chapters.title: Midnight Shift Change
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The Nickelsdorf checkpoint: between 23:40 and 00:10, the night shift overlaps and identity checks lapse. Ilse walks Wren through her plan, revealing she's crossed this border four times under four names. The beat is intimacy through tradecraft — two people who trust each other only because they've both been forged.

chapters.title: Vasik's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vasik's POV. The handler's betrayal laid bare: he built the phantom flight to make Wren the deniable architect of an assassination, trading them upward for his own survival. He orders the checkpoint sealed early. The beat is cold ambition — the machinery of the Section grinding a person into an entry in a ledger.

chapters.title: Everything the Records Forgot
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Climax. At the checkpoint, with the seal descending early, Wren triggers the one weapon they have: Heller's true archive, broadcast to every desk in the Section — exposing Vasik's forgery and, deliberately, their own erased past. Ilse crosses in the confusion. Wren is taken. The beat is sacrifice as self-creation: burning the false self to keep one true act.

chapters.title: A Person of No Nation
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, weeks later. Ilse testifies from safety; Vasik is disavowed into the same nonexistence he dealt others. Wren, officially never employed, receives a postcard with no signature — just a birthday that now exists in one registry only: Ilse's memory. The beat is quiet belonging: identity kept alive by being remembered by someone.
